title: AppCritIQ Security Check
description: Schema for a single security check record, built from two sources only: (1) capabilities.csv's own columns (ID, Platform, CapabilityType, Category, Title, Description, Default Severity, NIAP, OWASP MASVS, OWASP MASWE, OWASP MASTG/MSTG, CVE, Phoenix Output Location), and (2) the field set AppCritIQ's own checks-conducted table already uses (Check, Result, Explanation, Compliance, Remediation, Evidence). No NowSecure-specific concepts and no cross-reference ID fields tied to an external source system. Not every field here is rendered in the PDF today -- this is meant as a complete data record a report template can choose to draw from.

check_id.description: Identifier for this check within your own catalog (e.g. a slug you assign). Not a cross-reference to any external system's row number.

title.description: Human-readable check name, matching capabilities.csv's Title column, e.g. 'Insecure or outdated cryptographic algorithms / implementations'.

category.description: Top-level grouping, matching capabilities.csv's Category column.

platform.description: Matches capabilities.csv's Platform column. Use 'Cross-platform' only in your own catalog if you've deliberately merged an iOS row and an Android row that describe the same underlying check.

capability_type.description: Which analysis input(s) the check runs against, matching capabilities.csv's CapabilityType column. A capability often has separate Binary and Source rows in the CSV -- list every type that applies to this check.

description.description: What the check looks for, in the abstract -- matches capabilities.csv's Description column, e.g. 'Detect weak, deprecated, or misused cryptographic algorithms and APIs such as MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC2/RC4, custom crypto, or improper encoding used as protection.'

status.description: Outcome of this check on a specific scan. Matches the 'Result' column in AppCritIQ's checks-conducted table. Use 'Not Evaluated' rather than guessing when the check didn't run or the tool didn't cover it, instead of defaulting to 'Not Present'.

severity.description: Matches capabilities.csv's Default Severity column. 'Variable' is used in the CSV itself for a few checks (e.g. 'Components with known vulnerabilities') where actual severity depends on the specific CVE found. 'N/A' is used for pure inventory/artifact checks that don't carry a risk rating of their own.

impact.description: Plain-language explanation of what happens if this check's status is 'Present' (i.e. the issue exists) -- matches the 'Explanation' column in AppCritIQ's checks-conducted table. Distinct from description: description explains what the check looks for in general; impact explains the consequence for this specific finding.

remediation.description: Matches the remediation-link field in AppCritIQ's checks-conducted table.

resources.description: Links to remediation guides, standards pages, or vendor documentation.

compliance.description: Every standards mapping capabilities.csv carries for a check, plus the additional tags (HIPAA/GDPR/legacy OWASP Mobile Top 10) that show up in the 'Compliance' column of AppCritIQ's own checks-conducted table. Populate whichever apply; leave the rest as empty arrays.

niap.description: NIAP Protection Profile requirement IDs, e.g. 'FDP_DEC_EXT.1.1'. Matches capabilities.csv's NIAP column (semicolon-separated in the source file -- split into array elements here).

owasp_masvs.description: OWASP MASVS control IDs, e.g. 'MASVS-CRYPTO-1'. Matches capabilities.csv's OWASP MASVS column.

owasp_maswe.description: OWASP MASWE weakness IDs, e.g. 'MASWE-0019'. Matches capabilities.csv's OWASP MASWE column.

owasp_mastg_mstg.description: Test IDs from capabilities.csv's combined 'OWASP MASTG / MSTG' column, e.g. 'CRYPTO/MASTG-TEST-0061' or the legacy 'MSTG-CRYPTO-4' -- the source column mixes both numbering schemes, so both live here as given.

owasp_top10_mobile_2016.description: Legacy OWASP Mobile Top 10 (2016) category, e.g. 'M5: Insufficient Cryptography'. Not a capabilities.csv column, but appears in AppCritIQ's own Compliance field for many checks and is worth carrying alongside MASVS.

cwe.description: CWE IDs, e.g. 'CWE-327'. Not a dedicated capabilities.csv column on its own, but shows up bundled into it for a handful of checks and consistently appears in AppCritIQ's Compliance field.

cve.description: Specific CVE IDs this check flags for, e.g. 'CVE-2014-0160'. Matches capabilities.csv's CVE column -- populated only for the small number of checks that target a named vulnerability (vulnerable OpenSSL/Nanopb versions).

hipaa.description: HIPAA citations, e.g. '164.312(a)(2)(iv)'. Not a capabilities.csv column, but appears in AppCritIQ's Compliance field for storage/transport-related checks.

gdpr.description: GDPR article references, e.g. 'Articles 5, 25, 32'. Same source as hipaa -- AppCritIQ's own Compliance field, not capabilities.csv.

evidence.description: Where the finding was (or would be) observed. Matches the 'Evidence' column in AppCritIQ's checks-conducted table, extended with capabilities.csv's Phoenix Output Location column (which tool produced the data and where in its raw output).

file_path.description: File or manifest location where the finding shows up, e.g. 'AndroidManifest.xml' or a specific source file path.

tool.description: Which scanning tool produced this evidence, per capabilities.csv's Phoenix Output Location column, e.g. 'mobsf', 'androguard', 'apktool', 'lief', 'strings', 'gitleaks', 'trufflehog', 'opengrep', 'syft', 'apksigner', or 'dynamic' for runtime-only checks.

output_location.description: Path/key within that tool's raw output, e.g. 'mobsf_scanner/mobsf_report.json:binary_analysis.findings'. Kept close to the raw capabilities.csv string for traceability rather than over-parsed.

report_section.description: Which AppCritIQ report section this check's result would render under, if displayed. Presentation-only -- everything above this field is source-of-truth data independent of any one report layout.
